rationale: Block 3 covers India's communicable disease burden including the major diseases. Checks recall of the current national TB programme name (NTEP replaced RNTCP in 2020).

Block 6 covers control measures at three prevention levels and national programmes (NTEP/NVBDCP/NLEP/NACO). Tests understanding of basic reproduction number (R0) and herd immunity threshold (HIT = 1 − 1/R0).
Block 5 covers modifiable behavioural risk factors for NCDs as identified by WHO. Tests recall of the four major modifiable risk factors.
Block 8 covers NCD programme monitoring including NPCDCS screening targets and HMIS reporting. Tests application of opportunistic screening principles from the NPCDCS mandate.
Block 6 covers PHC-level case management for NTEP, NVBDCP, NLEP, NACO, and UIP. Tests application of correct programme-specific protocols — specifically the UIP routine immunisation schedule.
Block 10 covers applying programme knowledge at the PHC simultaneously — the clinical pearl that a patient can belong to multiple programmes. Tests understanding of programme co-enrolment.
Block 3 covers epidemic definitions and types (common-source vs propagated). Tests understanding of epidemic curve interpretation.
Block 6 covers the 10-step outbreak investigation framework and the principle that control measures should begin while investigation is ongoing. Tests application of this key principle.
Block 5 covers determinants of surveillance quality and failure. Tests understanding of IDSP reporting form types and who completes each.
Block 8 covers health information systems and HMIS/DHIS2. Tests evaluation of zero reporting as a data quality indicator — a nuanced concept covered in the clinical pearl.
